title: Umm Sulaym
hookLine: who accepted faith as her dowry, and bore a grief with remarkable patience (Bukhari)

cards: A man of Medina named Abu Talhah comes to ask a woman to marry him. The woman is Umm Sulaym, the mother of Anas, the boy who served the Prophet. She has become Muslim.

He has not. When the talk turns to a dowry, she names one, and it isn't anything he can carry in his hands. Today: Umm Sulaym, in two scenes, one at the start of a marriage and one in the middle of it.

teach.h: IF YOU ACCEPT ISLAM, THAT IS MY DOWRY.
teach.b: The first scene is in the Sunan of al-Nasa'i. Umm Sulaym answered Abu Talhah that a man like him was not someone to turn away, but she was a Muslim and he was not, and she could not marry him as things were.
If you accept Islam, she said, that will be my dowry, and I'll ask you for nothing else. He accepted Islam, and that was her dowry. The second scene, in Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim, is hard.

teach.h: THE BOY DIED WHILE HE WAS OUT.
teach.b: Their young son was ill, and while Abu Talhah was out, the boy died. Umm Sulaym prepared the child, laid him aside, and told the household not to tell his father until she did.

teach.h: HE IS CALMER; I HOPE HE IS AT REST.
teach.b: When Abu Talhah came home and asked about the boy, she said he was calmer than he had been, and she hoped he was at rest. She brought him his supper. They spent the night together.
In the morning, she told him. Sahih Muslim adds how: if people lent something to a family and then asked for it back, would the family have the right to refuse? No, he said.
Then, she said, seek your reward from God for your son. He went to the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, and told him everything, and the Prophet prayed for blessing on their night together.
Readers take this story in different ways. Some see astonishing patience.
Some find it hard to read. Both reactions sit honestly with it. What is clear is that she chose her moment, let her husband eat and rest, and gave him the news in a picture he could hold.

how: Muslims tell Umm Sulaym's story from al-Nasa'i, where her dowry is Abu Talhah's Islam, and from Bukhari and Muslim, where she breaks the news of their son's death; at a loss, Muslims say inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un.

o: Anas's mother, who asked for Islam as her dowry
Anas's grandmother, who raised him in Medina
a wife of the Prophet who lost a young son

p: her son, who served the Prophet
her picture of the son's death

s: Umm Sulaym asked Abu Talhah for a large gift of gold
al-Nasa'i says she asked only for his Islam, and nothing else.
she told her husband about their son as soon as he came home
she let him eat and rest, and told him in the morning.
the Prophet prayed for blessing on their night
Bukhari keeps his prayer after Abu Talhah told him.

games.q: you are Umm Sulaym. your son has died while your husband was out. he walks in tired and asks how the boy is. what do you do?
o: tell him at once, at the door.
say the boy is calmer, feed him, and tell him in the morning.
send someone else to tell him.
games.why: Bukhari says she said he was calmer and she hoped he was at rest, served supper, and told him in the morning, as a loan returned.

practice: This one can be gentle. Bring to mind one hard thing you're carrying, not the hardest, one you can look at, and hold it the way you'd hold something fragile, without pushing it away.
If you pray, you can say what Muslims say at a loss: inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un, to God we belong and to Him we return.

wordCard.voice: Umm Sulaym. The mother of Anas, who asked for Islam as her dowry and told her husband of their son's death in a picture of a loan returned. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: Umm Sulaym, mother of Sulaym, the name she is known by.

carryVoice: Your line: faith for a dowry. Hard news, given with care. That's day eight hundred fifty.
